item.description: The review fast path asks for expectation, actual behavior, why, and consequence as a callout on the responsible element, never manufactured.
item.label: Calling out surprises is a step

item.description: reviewstate lists each slide's callout Items with label, body, and the Item they are about, as callouts in JSON.
item.label: Callouts in the review report

item.description: Each slide prints its surprises, and each review counts them; the count is reported, never required.
item.label: review list names surprises

item.description: A collapsible Surprises panel on each slide; a callout's panel is labelled Surprise with its body and a link to its element.
item.label: Surprises in the viewer

item.body: You would expect a callout's text to reach the reviewer; before this change the viewer rendered only its label and description, so the expected-versus-actual body never showed.
item.description: Why the viewer change matters: callouts existed but their point was hidden.
item.label: A callout's body was invisible

item.description: The page shows the Surprises panel, panel body and about link; review list and JSON name callouts; a browser test sees the panel on the slide.
item.label: Viewer and list tests

slide.takeaway: A callout Item is a surprise: the report carries it, review list names it, and the viewer shows it in a panel on the slide and in its element's panel.
slide.title: Surprises reach the reviewer
